Made in China. Make sure your expectations are not too high. - The listing pictures are a little misleading for this icemaker. It is not overflowing at the top as it shows. Once the ice reaches the top of the basket, it will stop making ice until you remove the ice.

Though it shows that this icemaker can make 26 ½ pounds of ice and 24 hours… That is also misleading. The only way you could do that is if you constantly remove the ice from the machine so that it can continue to make more. You would have to remove it at least once an hour if not more frequently.

The ice is “wet”. So if you remove it and then place it in your freezer, it will stick together. So it’s best to place it in a bag so you can easily whack it to break it apart.

I like this icemaker overall for what it is. But I think if your expectations are too high then you will be disappointed.

Make sure to keep water in as instructed, and residual lint is gathered within the container. I then dump the water into my utility sink and catch the lint in the drain strainer.
The down side to this solution is that all of the heat venting from the dryer stay in my laundry room. Since the laundry room is not part of my AC system, this is not really a problem. But it is a consideration for other situations.
As mentioned, my long term solution is to re-route the ductwork. But this is keeping the fire hazard under control in the mean time.

Seems to work, simple to use - We've had our pedestal humidifier for 3 weeks, and have been very pleased with it so far. I've added the bacteriostatic solution 2-3 times a week, and so far haven't noticed any musty smells.

We live in northern Colorado, and it's very dry, and we've been running the humidifier continuously since we got it. I haven't noticed any adverse effects on the wick from using the bacteriostatic solution. Prior to first using the bacteriostatic solution, the wick developed a brownish area on the topmost air intake side of the wick, about 1/5 of the wick size. The wick remained wet there. After a week or so, I rotated the wick so that the brown portion was in the water bath, and the brown color went away. The new topmost air intake side turned brown just like before, but was still wet. Using the bacteriostatic solution hasn't had any impact on the brown area, or how wet the wick gets.

The solution has chemical product warnings on it, and says to add "1/8 of a capful to a gallon of water." The active ingredient to the solution is an ammonia compound, so safety warnings are appropriate. Measuring 1/8 of a capful is an approximate measurement, and that doesn't present much of a challenge if you add about that much to the cap once, see about how much that is, and thereafter add that amount directly to the water you're adding.
